{{Short description|Economic model}}
In [[spatial analysis]], the '''Huff model''' is a widely used tool for predicting the probability of a consumer visiting a site, as a function of the distance of the site, its attractiveness, and the relative attractiveness of alternatives. It was formulated by David Huff in 1963.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Huff|first=David L.|date=1963|title=A Probabilistic Analysis of Shopping Center Trade Areas|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3144521|journal=Land Economics|volume=39|issue=1|pages=81–90|doi=10.2307/3144521|jstor=3144521 |issn=0023-7639|url-access=subscription}}</ref> It is used in marketing, economics, retail research and urban planning,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Huff, David {{!}} AAG|url=http://www.aag.org/cs/membership/tributes_memorials/gl/huff_david|access-date=2021-04-20|website=www.aag.org|archive-date=2021-04-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210422182049/http://www.aag.org/cs/membership/tributes_memorials/gl/huff_david|url-status=dead}}</ref> and is implemented in several commercially available GIS systems.

Its relative ease of use and applicability to a wide range of problems contribute to its enduring appeal.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Dramowicz|first=Ela|title=Retail Trade Area Analysis Using the Huff Model|url=https://www.directionsmag.com/article/3207|access-date=2021-04-20|website=www.directionsmag.com|publication-date=2005-07-03}}</ref>

The formula is given as:

<math>P_{ij}=
\frac{A_j^\alpha D_{ij}^{- \beta}}
{\sum_{k=1}^{n}A_k^{\alpha} D_{ik}^{- \beta}}
</math>

where :

* <math>A_j</math> is a measure of the attractiveness of store ''j''
* <math>D_{ij}</math> is the distance from the consumer's location, ''i'', to store ''j''.
* <math>\alpha</math> is an attractiveness parameter
* <math>\beta</math> is a distance decay parameter
* <math>n</math> is the total number of stores, including store ''j''
